summary: Growing up in a rural farming family in India, I have seen how sudden weather changes or bad soil conditions can ruin an entire season's crop. When that happens, my father and other farmers like him struggle to earn a fair living, and the whole family feels that stress. I built this app to give farmers simple, clear information before they plant or sell. Using NASA satellite and weather data, the app shows farmers the exact weather updates and soil type in their area so they can protect their crops and plan ahead. It also has an easy AI chat where farmers can ask everyday questions, along with live local market (mandi) prices so they know when and where to sell their harvest for a good profit. My goal is to put helpful tools directly into farmers' hands so they can avoid crop losses, earn what they deserve, and support their families.
details: FarmShift India is a lightweight, farmer-first web application built by Team City Rats </3 for the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge. Growing up in a rural farming family in India, I have seen firsthand how sudden weather shifts, mismatched soil conditions, or unclear post-harvest costs can ruin an entire season's harvest and place heavy financial stress on families. FarmShift addresses this by bringing NASA Earth observations, local weather forecasts, and practical rupee-first farm calculators together into one calm, mobile-friendly workspace available across 13 Indian languages, including English, Punjabi, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Urdu, Odia, and Assamese. Using browser geolocation or village and district search—piloted with Ludhiana, Punjab—FarmShift retrieves recent regional temperature and meteorological context from the NASA POWER Daily API, displays satellite imagery layers through NASA GIBS (including MODIS True Colour, Vegetation/NDVI, Land Temperature, and SMAP Soil Moisture), and offers a direct launch point into NASA Worldview. It pairs these space-based observations with a 10-day forecast from Open-Meteo to power an interactive Crop and Water Planner that evaluates crop-rotation options across five transparent signals: water availability, soil type, heat, weather, and crop diversity. Beyond planting decisions, the workspace brings together practical prototype tools for the full farming cycle, including MandiMitra for calculating net mandi returns after transport and handling costs, a Farm Budget break-even calculator, KhetSlot for planning machinery requests alongside Government FARMS, CropCare for organizing crop symptoms and field photos for agricultural experts, HarvestLink for post-harvest coordination, quick access to official schemes like myScheme and PM Fasal Bima Yojana, and a guided rules-based Ask FarmShift assistant. The main benefit of FarmShift India is that it removes the technical, financial, and language barriers that normally lock smallholder farmers out of space and climate data. By running as a zero-install web app with an instant Guest Mode, farmers can check regional satellite context, compare crop options, and calculate mandi net returns immediately without creating an account or downloading heavy software. Our intended impact is to put trustworthy, easy-to-understand field and market intelligence directly into farmers' hands so they can reduce preventable crop losses, manage input and transport expenses, and earn a fairer living for their families while staying connected to verified human experts such as ICAR, PAU, and Kisan Call Centres. To build the project, we used pure HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript in a dependency-free static architecture hosted on GitHub Pages so the app loads quickly even on slow rural mobile networks. On the data and backend side, we integrated the NASA POWER Daily API, NASA GIBS imagery services, NASA Worldview, and the Open-Meteo Forecast API, alongside a 13-language translation selector and a security-ready backend schema built for Supabase Authentication, PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security for private per-user cloud sync, and Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA protection. In accordance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, we also disclose that generative AI tools were used to help organize our pitch deck narrative, refine UI copy, and structure project documentation, whereas the in-app Ask FarmShift assistant currently operates using transparent local rules rather than an unverified generative AI model. What makes FarmShift India creative is its Blue Ocean approach: rather than building another dense GIS dashboard for researchers or an opaque black-box AI predictor, we designed a clean, Pinterest-inspired card workspace tailored specifically to Indian rural workflows. Every insight follows a strict traceability principle—moving from NASA signal to local farm context to human verification—while pairing space observations with rupee-first calculators that reflect real decisions farmers make before sowing and before traveling to a mandi. Throughout development, our team carefully considered scientific integrity, rural connectivity, user privacy, and linguistic safety. We explicitly framed our crop-rotation scores as transparent planning heuristics rather than yield guarantees, and we clearly labeled sample equipment listings and editable market quotes as illustrative prototypes so farmers never mistake demo placeholders for live commercial offers. We prioritized Guest Mode by default so browser-level work stays private without mandatory sign-ups, and we noted that automated translations of agricultural and safety guidance require native-speaker agronomy review before real-world deployment.
